releaseNotes: Sharded the audit's two dominant serial steps inside their own runners. launchbench's validator fixture suite (validation/repository/run-validator-fixtures.ts, 18 domain modules, ~730 spawned validator runs) and test:fixtures (verification/fixtures/run.ts, auto-discovered suites) previously executed every fixture as a one-at-a-time spawnSync tsx child, so ~0.35s of per-process boot per run made them ~90% of the audit's wall time. Each runner now re-spawns itself once per module/suite through a shared worker pool (tooling/lib/shard-pool.ts, width min(cores-2, 8), B2C_FIXTURE_CONCURRENCY overrides, 1 is the kill switch), starts the heaviest module first so a large module registered late cannot extend the tail alone, and prints one combined report in registration order — the output keeps the serial run's shape and order. Individual fixture executions are never pooled: modules reuse and mutate fixture roots between runs, so the module is the isolation boundary; --serial and --keep-temp preserve the old in-process behavior.

Made the shard result contract fail-closed and tested. A shard child reports its results as JSON on a marker line; a child that dies before printing the marker is reported as a failed row in the combined report — never as empty-and-passing. verification/fixtures/audit.fixtures.ts now proves the three load-bearing properties: parseShardOutput distinguishes crashed-before-reporting (results undefined) from reported results, an unknown --shard name exits non-zero with a named error, and launchbench plus test:fixtures stay serial:true in both audit-plan layouts because their parallelism lives inside the runner — riding the 4-wide audit pool too would multiply the process fan-out.
